name: Visual Appeal of Helsinki Streets: 360° panorama rating
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (64 new Google Street View 360° panorama strips of Helsinki, captured 2017–2026, © Google). Based on Malekzadeh, Willberg, Torkko, Korpilo, Hasanzadeh, Järv & Toivonen, "Do Street View Imagery and Public Participation GIS align: Comparative Analysis of Urban Attractiveness" (arXiv:2511.05570). Participants read the paper's instruction sheet (rate permanent qualities such as architecture, green space, walkability, urban design and upkeep; ignore weather, temporary objects and people), then rate 40 panoramas for "visual appeal" from 1 (least) to 7 (most). In the paper, 24 raters gave 24,349 ratings to 1,967 Helsinki panoramas (≥500 each, about 11 ratings per image, Cronbach's alpha 0.94); a segmentation-based model was then compared with PPGIS places residents marked as attractive or unattractive.

Differences from the original study: (1) 40 panoramas per participant instead of at least 500; (2) images are 64 random Street View locations, not the paper's 1,967 (random plus PPGIS-matched) locations from 2009–2017; (3) our panoramas are equirectangular strips centred on the capture direction, while the paper stitched six 60° views starting at north; (4) one question on whether the participant lives in Helsinki was added (the paper recruited both residents and non-residents).
author: Malekzadeh, Willberg, Torkko, Korpilo, Hasanzadeh, Järv & Toivonen
